newsitem.title: USA: Fund managers remain neutral on US debt -- survey.
newsitem.headline: Fund managers remain neutral on US debt -- survey.

text.p: Money managers kept U.S. debt portfolios relatively unchanged over the past week, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"For the second consecutive week, money managers ... made no substantive change in portfolio structures," the report said.
"Activity appeared to have been both fairly limited and two-way," it said.
In the week ended June 3, the cash/assets ratio fell to 9.09 percent from 9.14 percent on an arithmetic basis and fell to 6.18 percent from 6.21 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index declined to 98.74 percent from 98.97 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 99.44 percent from 98.99 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index held steady at 4.78 on an arithmetic basis. It fell to 4.38 from 4.71 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Thirteen percent of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from nil in the week ending May 27.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
